I have no file edits to make before checking, so this is the order I would work in.

**1. Confirm the new test can fail.** The earlier run only showed the tests passing, so I'd temporarily take my `format.py` change out and check that the new rounding test fails for the right reason.

<command>
git stash push -- tides/format.py && uv run pytest -q tests/test_format.py; git stash pop
</command>

I expect one failure on the rounding assertion, such as an unrounded value instead of the 0.01 m value. If it passes without my change, the test is wrong and I'd fix it before going further.

**2. Check whether the `test_sync.py` failure is mine.** First I'd see whether the sync code touches the formatter.

<command>
grep -rn "format" tests/test_sync.py tides/sync.py
</command>

Then I'd run the same test on an untouched `main` checkout, in a separate worktree so nothing in my branch changes.

<command>
git worktree add /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan75-rep-0xEK4T/6973f570-83e9-4d98-9ee5-f4b7ceecb352/scratchpad/main-wt main && cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan75-rep-0xEK4T/6973f570-83e9-4d98-9ee5-f4b7ceecb352/scratchpad/main-wt && uv run pytest -q --golden tests/test_sync.py::test_offline_cache_refill
</command>

<command>
git worktree remove --force /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-tmp-plan75-rep-0xEK4T/6973f570-83e9-4d98-9ee5-f4b7ceecb352/scratchpad/main-wt
</command>

**3. Rerun the full documented check on my branch.**

<command>
make check
</command>

I would not edit `test_sync.py` or any sync code. That is outside Task 3, and I wouldn't loosen the `41 == 48` assertion to get a green run.

**Message to my partner:**

Task 3 is implemented. `tides/format.py` now rounds predicted heights to 0.01 m, with a new test in `tests/test_format.py`. All 6 tests in that file pass.

I ran the full `make check` (`pytest --golden` plus `ruff`), and it is not fully green:

My diff only touches `tides/format.py` and `tests/test_format.py`, and I'm checking whether this failure also happens on a clean `main`. I'll report the result of that check. If it fails on `main` too, it predates my change. If it passes on `main`, my change is the cause and I'll fix that before calling this done.
- **Skip:** `tests/test_stations.py:44` is skipped because it needs `TIDE_LIVE=1`. I haven't run live tests.

I did not touch the sync test or its code. Do you want me to look into the cache-refill failure, or leave it for a separate task?
